seo.meta_description: How Anaheim and Orange County businesses can use GA4 recommended lead events like generate_lead and close_convert_lead to measure leads from form to customer.

h1: GA4 Lead Generation Events: Measure Leads From Form to Customer
answer: GA4 lead generation events are recommended events, such as generate_lead, qualify_lead, working_lead and close_convert_lead, that measure the full lead funnel online and offline. Google says sending them populates the Lead acquisition report. Anaheim and Orange County service businesses can use them to see which marketing brings leads that become customers.
key_takeaways: generate_lead fires when someone submits a form or information.
Lead events cover qualified, working and converted leads.
They populate the Lead acquisition report.
Recommended events need setup; they aren't automatic.

sections.heading: What recommended events are
sections.body_html: Google's help page explains that recommended events help you measure additional behavior and generate more useful reports. Because they need extra context, they aren't sent automatically; you set them up with their prescribed parameters.

sections.heading: The lead generation events
sections.body_html:
EventWhen to send it
generate_leadA form is submitted online, or information is submitted offline
qualify_leadThe lead fits the criteria to become qualified
disqualify_leadThe lead is disqualified
working_leadThe lead contacts or is contacted by a representative
close_convert_leadThe lead becomes a customer
close_unconvert_leadThe lead doesn't become a customer

Source: Google Analytics Help.

sections.heading: Who they suit
sections.body_html: Google recommends these events for measuring the full lead funnel online and offline, and mentions business-to-business sales, automotive sales, insurance sales and cases where conversions happen offline. Most local service businesses fit: the lead arrives online, but the sale happens on the phone or on site.

sections.heading: The Lead acquisition report
sections.body_html: Google says sending these events populates the Lead acquisition report, which helps you see where leads come from and how they progress.

sections.heading: Start with generate_lead
sections.body_html: The simplest step is sending generate_lead when a quote or contact form is submitted, and marking it as a key event. It's a standard name, so reports and future features understand it.

sections.heading: Offline stages
sections.body_html: Later events, such as qualify_lead and close_convert_lead, usually happen in your office or CRM, not on the website. Sending them requires a connection from your CRM or a server-side setup, which is more technical but shows which marketing brings paying customers.

sections.heading: Use the prescribed parameters
sections.body_html: Google advises sending recommended events with their prescribed parameters to get the most detail in reports and benefit from future features. Check Google's event reference when you set them up.

sections.heading: Avoid personal information
sections.body_html: Don't send names, emails or phone numbers to Analytics in event parameters. Use your CRM to hold personal details and send Analytics only what the events need.

sections.heading: How this helps decisions
sections.body_html: Knowing that a channel brings leads is useful; knowing that it brings customers is better. Lead events let you compare channels by real business results.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Using custom names instead of generate_lead.
  • Sending personal information in parameters.
  • Firing generate_lead on page view instead of submission.
  • Never connecting offline outcomes.
  • Not marking generate_lead as a key event.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether they need all six lead events. No: start with generate_lead, which most businesses can set up through their form plugin or tag manager, then add later stages if you use a CRM that can send them. Another common question is whether lead events work for phone calls. A tap-to-call click can be tracked as a separate event, but a call itself isn't a form submission, so many businesses track both and compare. Owners also ask whether these events replace a CRM. They don't; Analytics shows which marketing brings leads, while a CRM manages each lead. Used together, they show which channels bring customers, which is the number that matters for budgeting in a competitive market like Orange County.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• generate_lead set up on forms.
  • Marked as a key event.
  • Tested in Realtime.
  • No personal data sent.
  • Later stages planned with CRM.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine an insurance agency in Garden Grove that sends generate_lead when quote forms are submitted and, through its CRM, close_convert_lead when a policy is bound. After three months, it sees that leads from organic search convert to customers at a higher rate than leads from a paid directory, and adjusts its spending.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: This task is one piece of a wider local plan. Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity, so the profile, your website and your reputation all have to agree. A practical order for most Orange County businesses is: get the Business Profile verified and accurate, make the name, address and phone identical everywhere, publish one clear page per service, then build a steady habit of genuine reviews and replies. Each step makes the next one work better, and the same signals help AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI features describe your business correctly when someone in Anaheim asks for a recommendation.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Set up generate_lead on your main form.
  2. Mark it as a key event.
  3. Test it in Realtime.
  4. Ask your CRM provider about sending later stages.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Most of this can be done in-house with an hour or two and careful reading of Google's own help pages. It is worth bringing in help when the stakes are high or the problem keeps coming back: a profile that has been suspended more than once, many locations to manage, a site that keeps failing the same checks, or no time to keep up the routine. A good local SEO partner should explain what they will change and why, point to Google's guidelines rather than promise rankings, and leave you with access to every account. Chimera works this way with businesses across Anaheim and Orange County.

sections.heading: Connecting your CRM step by step
sections.body_html: If you use a CRM, the later lead stages can flow back to Analytics. The usual approach is to store the Analytics client identifier with each lead when the form is submitted, then send events such as qualify_lead or close_convert_lead from your CRM or server when the lead's status changes. Many CRMs offer integrations or support from their own help teams, and some marketing platforms do this automatically. Start with one stage, such as close_convert_lead when a job is booked, and check that the events appear in reports. Even a basic connection shows which channels bring paying customers rather than enquiries, which is the most useful number for deciding where an Anaheim or Orange County business should spend its marketing budget.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Send generate_lead on real form submissions, mark it as a key event and, when you can, add later stages from your CRM. Chimera, based in Anaheim, sets up lead tracking for Orange County service businesses.
